PD-LMI

MATLAB / YALMIP

PD-LMI

Parameter-dependent LMIs, represented cell by cell.

Model continuous piecewise-polynomial matrix functions on physical grid cells using a cell-local tensor-product Bernstein basis. Use DPD-LMI only when the model explicitly includes differentiable decisions and bounded parameter rates.

From one quadratic two-cell DPD-LMI to finite constraints

Read the geometry first. Each step keeps a short explanation, a runnable API example, and a direct link into the detailed manual.

01

Form the DPD-LMI

xᵢ(ρ) are parameter-dependent decision functions; known matrix functions multiply them and their scheduling derivatives.

F(ρ,ρ˙)=∑i=1NRi(ρ)∑s=1ℓ∂xi∂ρs(ρ)ρ˙s+F0(ρ)+∑i=1NFi(ρ)xi(ρ)≺0.\mathcal F(\rho,\dot\rho)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}R_i(\rho)\sum_{s=1}^{\ell}\frac{\partial x_i}{\partial\rho_s}(\rho)\dot\rho_s+F_0(\rho)+\sum_{i=1}^{N}F_i(\rho)x_i(\rho)\prec0.F(ρ,ρ˙​)=i=1∑N​Ri​(ρ)s=1∑ℓ​∂ρs​∂xi​​(ρ)ρ˙​s​+F0​(ρ)+i=1∑N​Fi​(ρ)xi​(ρ)≺0.

02

Grid the ρ\rhoρ-space

The concrete known matrix A below lives on two physical hypercubes. Click either cell to inspect its domain and the exact degree-two local coefficient matrices stored under its LocalValues leaf.

grid = {[0 0.5 1], [0 1]};
A = pdmat(grid, @(r1,r2) [1+r1+r2 r1*r2; r1*r2 2+r1^2], Degree=2);
A.cells()
A.LocalValues{c1}{1}
Open the detailed manual section ↗
03

Build constraints inside each hypercube

Map every physical cell to local coordinates α∈[0,1]ℓ\alpha\in[0,1]^\ellα∈[0,1]ℓ, form the DPD-LMI residual there, and enumerate each admissible rate vertex v. The result is one local polynomial-matrix inequality for every cell-and-rate pair.

αs=ρs−ρs(cs)ρs(cs+1)−ρs(cs)∈[0,1],∀s=1,…,ℓ.\alpha_s=\frac{\rho_s-\rho_s^{(c_s)}}{\rho_s^{(c_s+1)}-\rho_s^{(c_s)}}\in[0,1],\quad\forall s=1,\ldots,\ell.αs​=ρs(cs​+1)​−ρs(cs​)​ρs​−ρs(cs​)​​∈[0,1],∀s=1,…,ℓ.
F(c,v)(α)⪯0∀ c.F^{(\mathbf c,v)}(\alpha)\preceq0\quad\forall\,\mathbf c.F(c,v)(α)⪯0∀c.
yalmip('clear')
P = pdvar(n, grid, "symmetric", Degree=2);
D = rhodiff(P, rateBounds);
L = D + P*A + A'*P <= -epsilon*eye(n);

04

Select a finite certificate

Choose one finite sufficient representation for the same stored residual. Direct coefficient tests are the default; Pólya elevation, Putinar box certificates, and the full-box preordering are explicit alternatives with different cost and strength.

F(c,v)(α)=∑i∈ImCi(c,v)Bim(α)⪯0.F^{(\mathbf c,v)}(\boldsymbol\alpha)=\sum_{\mathbf i\in\mathcal I_m}C_{\mathbf i}^{(\mathbf c,v)}B_{\mathbf i}^{m}(\boldsymbol\alpha)\preceq0.F(c,v)(α)=i∈Im​∑​Ci(c,v)​Bim​(α)⪯0.
selected = L;                         % direct
selected = L.applyPolya(p);           % Pólya elevation p
selected = L.applyPutinar();          % Putinar
selected = L.applyFullBoxPreorder();  % full box
Open the detailed manual section ↗
05

Export, solve, and recover the decision matrix

Export the finite constraints to YALMIP, call the selected solver, and evaluate the optimized decision matrix. The recovered matrix function uses the same grid, cell ordering, and Bernstein storage created at the start.

constraints = selected.toYalmip();
diagnostics = optimize(constraints, objective, options);
assert(diagnostics.problem == 0)
Psol = value(P);
